newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek yield curve shifts up, tax unnnerves market.
newsitem.headline: Greek yield curve shifts up, tax unnnerves market.

text.p: Greek markets were nervous with depos and forex swaps trading higher 30 to 40 basis points in late dealings on a combination of forex outflows and concern about the impact of a possible tax on FRNs and derivatives.
"Depos and forex forwards are up 30 to 40 basis points on forex outflows and concern about the impact of a likely tax on outstanding FRNs and derivatives," said a trader at a foreign bank.

Forex outflows valued at a total of 250 million ecus took place at the fixing, driving ecu/drachma over the 302 drachma level. Lighter buying of forex for drachmas continued after the fixing prompting the central bank to put a lid on ecu/drachma in its afternoon intervention.
The central bank also intervened on both the bid and offer side in overnight funds at 12.40 percent and 13.40 percent respectively.

Traders said the thorny issue was whether the government would choose to tax outstanding FRNs. A high-level national economy ministry official said the government was leaning against taxing outstanding FRNs.
The mark was quoted at 157.36/41 drachmas from Monday's 157.530 fix, the dollar at 238.36/41 drachmas from 238.210 and the Ecu at 301.79/89 from 302.120 drachmas.
